text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima to push for tough penalties against Austria's provinces so as not to endanger Austria's entry into the European Monetary Union.
- Klima to decide in first half of this week on whether to accept the consortium's bid for Creditanstalt.

- Peter Gaugg, chief executive of the Bank fuer Tirol und Vorarlberg, member of the takeover consortium of Creditanstalt, expects Klima to call for a new round of bids, but expects the consortium to still have a good chance.
- Austria has gambled away its advantage in the emerging countries as other countries are catching up fast. The idea of Austria being a centre for the region within the European Union has been lost.
- "The European Monetary Union will start in 1999 as planned", Klima said.
- Austrian President Thomas Klestil is suffering from a severe case of viral pneumonia. He will probably stay another few weeks in hospital.
- A study shows that while antisemitism is still very strong in Austria, xenophobia and tolerance are quite balanced.
- A new call for bids for the government's stake in Creditanstalt will likely be announced as the consortium's offer is not seen as satisfactory.
